items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter names throughout the core logic: `m`, `q`, `d`, `s`, `o` (e.g. `s = (d@q.T).ravel()`, `o = np.argsort(-s)`). Statements are chained with `;` on one line. No named constants for the model, revision, query or k. Still short and easy to follow.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Throwaway script that was deleted afterwards (`rm /app/emb.py`). Model, revision, query and rank are literals, not named constants. A debug loop prints the top 7 (`for i in o[:7]: print(...)`). Fine for a one-off, but it doesn't follow the named-constants convention.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Files are opened without context managers (`open("/app/result.txt","w").write(...)`). Magic numbers 4 and 7 are inline. No tie assertion. Blank lines are filtered and the encoding is set explicitly. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Ranking details handled correctly
items.evidence: Pins the revision and uses query/passage prompt types. Ranks by cosine on normalised vectors, descending, and takes `o[4]`. Removes only the trailing newline (`rstrip("\n")`) and filters blank lines. There is no tie check, though the agent printed the scores and pointed out the 0.003 gap.
